stem: Which statement about OSHA labeling of blood or other potentially infectious material (OPIM) specimens is accurate?

options.A: A recognizable specimen container may be exempt from individual labeling while it remains within a facility that uses Universal Precautions, but required labeling or color-coding applies when the specimen leaves the facility
options.B: Every individual specimen tube must always carry its own biohazard label even when it is placed inside a properly labeled secondary container
options.C: Specimen labeling is required only when the patient is known to have a bloodborne infection
options.D: Blood and OPIM specimens never require labeling or color-coding during transport or shipping

rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 states that blood or OPIM specimens must be placed in leak-preventing containers. A facility that uses Universal Precautions for all specimens may omit specimen labeling/color-coding while recognizable specimen containers remain within the facility. That exemption does not apply when specimens leave the facility. OSHA also permits individual containers to be exempt when placed inside an appropriately labeled or color-coded larger container. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Apply OSHA's specimen-container labeling rule and recognize the limited within-facility Universal Precautions exemption.
source_locator: §1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(A): specimen containment and within-facility Universal Precautions labeling exemption; §1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(A)-(G): labels/color coding and exceptions
source_claim_supported: Recognizable specimen containers can be exempt from individual labeling within a facility using Universal Precautions, but the exemption does not extend to specimens leaving the facility; appropriately labeled larger containers can also satisfy the labeling requirement for enclosed individual containers.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: follow procedures for handling biohazardous and hazardous materials; apply infection-prevention principles
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — blood/OPIM specimen handling and labeling
correction_summary: Corrected the source item's false universal claim that every laboratory specimen requires its own biohazard label. Reframed the item around OSHA's actual labeling rule and its within-facility Universal Precautions and secondary-container exceptions.
audit_findings: A accurately states OSHA's exception structure. B ignores the larger labeled-container exception; C incorrectly ties labeling to known patient infection status; D contradicts transport/shipping requirements. No second-answer ambiguity or unresolved regulatory conflict remains.
